page: UpCloud GPU-96xCPU-1920GB-8xH100 is a high-density, GPU-accelerated server designed for massive parallel computing workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 96 shared vCPUs and 1920.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 20.0 GB per vCPU. The primary hardware highlight is the integration of eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 640 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage options. The shared CPU allocation model indicates that while the raw compute capacity of the 96 vCPUs is substantial, the primary processing power is intended to be offloaded to the dedicated NVIDIA Hopper GPUs. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized, high-capital hardware class designed to maximize GPU compute density per node, making it a highly consolidated resource for enterprise-scale acceleration tasks.

Given the massive GPU memory and compute capabilities, this server is engineered for demanding workloads such as large language model training, complex deep learning, high-performance data science jobs, and distributed AI inference. It is also suitable for large-scale scientific simulations and parallel rendering tasks that require substantial GPU acceleration and a large system memory footprint.
